svg.text: ONE ROOF A DEVICE, ONE FRAME A NODE
The graph's blocks are the rack's frames, as many as PipeWire has; a device only gathers them under one roof.
1 · THE RACK, ONE FRAME A NODE
This machine now. A device: every node of one program or one piece of hardware. A frame: one node, all its ports. A cord: one link.
NO NODES: THE CARD'S PROFILE IS OFF. NOTHING TO PLUG.
A frame in its kind's colour, its jacks in their groups' (section 4). Under a frame: its media.class. A bracket under frames: one chain of a program's.
Not on the rack: Patchcord's own meters (16 nodes), the Dummy and Freewheel drivers (no ports). Both are in ENGINE.
2 · DEVICES: THREE ROOFS, EVERY NODE UNDER ONE
Asked in this order, so each node gets exactly one answer.
if the node has a device.id
a card, a Bluetooth headset, a USB interface, a camera
kind from device.api / device.form-factor: CARD, BLUETOOTH, USB, CAMERA
here: RYZEN, RADEON, JLAB GO WORK 2
if its client is a program: application.name + binary + pid
everything a program made: streams, sinks, filters, nodes without a class
kind APP; same names numbered by the client's object.serial
here: EASY EFFECTS, FOOYIN, HYDROGEN, KADENCE, SOUNDCRAFT
if neither: PipeWire or WirePlumber made it
a MIDI bridge, a null sink, a loopback, a filter-chain
· Off the rack, in the HIDDEN list and ENGINE: Patchcord's own nodes (its meters, the cue: the tool, not the graph), and a Bluetooth headset's
internal capture stream (WirePlumber's plumbing behind its MIC: in A2DP its input waits for a mic that isn't a node yet).
3 · JACKS: WHAT A PORT CAN BE
Four facts of a port: its direction, format.dsp, port.monitor and audio.channel. A jack shows them all.
direction in, 32 bit float mono audio
STEREO when FL and FR go alike; L, R; MONO; FC, LFE, AUX0…
the same labels; a capture source rings blue, a playback sink teal
a copy of what goes in: a sink's, and a recording stream's
8 bit raw midi, or 32 bit raw UMP
named by its client when a bridge carries many (MIDI THROUGH, HYDROGEN)
a format.dsp Patchcord doesn't know, or none
plugged as is, ringed in NO CLASS's sand: never hidden
· So: three media (audio, MIDI, video) and a fallback, in two directions, and the monitor flag on audio out. Which zone a jack sits in says
its direction; its ring says its media; its label says its channel or its client. A port is a mult: one jack per cord, one always free.
4 · FRAMES: A FRAME IS ITS BLOCK
One frame a node, in its kind's colour, as ENGINE's block. Its jacks in their groups' colours: IN at the left, OUT at the right, a monitor beside its input.
a card's or a program's: IN and its MONITOR
an app recording: IN and its MONITOR, its GAIN
an effect: IN, OUT, no volume
a bridge: a jack a client each way
a camera: OUT, no meter, no volume
a synth: MIDI in, audio out
The frame's outline and band on the rack; the block's outline and cap in ENGINE. By media.class, whoever owns it: the paint says that.
a card's output; a program's virtual sink
a mic; a program's virtual source
the ALSA MIDI bridge, BLE MIDI
in and out alike: Bitwig, a JACK app
Easy Effects' effects, its test signal
The jack's ring on the rack; the port's dot and pill in ENGINE. A group: the ports of one direction and one kind; on a MIDI bridge, of one client (one colour).
· One table of colours for ENGINE and the rack: a block's by its kind (eight), a port's by its group (seven). A block's colour is its main group's where it has one.
· A frame never splits: a node's inputs, outputs and monitor are one frame on one device. Two groups of one kind (a bridge's clients) share a colour; names tell them apart.
· Each audio group has its meter; a stereo one its SPLIT. A node with a volume (Props) has VOLUME (GAIN on a source or a recording), BAL if stereo, MUTE.
· GRAPH, on each frame's band before its name, with its node's id: ENGINE opens with that block chosen (in the LCD's amber) and in view. A frame is a block.
5 · DEVICE COLOURS: ONE PAINT A KIND
Three kinds, three paints (paints.py, variant D). A paint says whose a device is; what its ports carry is on its frames.
if the node has a device.id
a card, a headset, a USB interface, a camera
here: RYZEN, RADEON, JLAB GO WORK 2
if its client is a program
here: EASY EFFECTS, FOOYIN, HYDROGEN, KADENCE, SOUNDCRAFT
if neither: PipeWire or WirePlumber made it
MIDI or audio, video, no class: all alike
· Lightness first: aluminium light, black dark, olive in between, so no two pass for each other; only olive has a hue, muted against the bands.
· No gap left: every node is one of the three kinds, so every device has one of the three paints. Navy and cream go.
· Every port is on the rack, a stream's monitor too: the rack can patch whatever PipeWire can link.
· Hydrogen's MIDI stays on the MIDI bridge's frame, beside its other clients: as on the graph.
· Passive links are cords like any other.
· Not now: node.link-group as a roof (linkgroup.py); a device is still its hardware, its program, or a node of its own.
· A headset's internal capture stream stays hidden (SYSTEM), as now: before the switch to HSP/HFP there is no mic to show it linked to.
